title: Harvinder Motors v. BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd.
one_line: Under Section 126 and the DERC Regulations, a case of 'dishonest abstraction of energy' cannot be booked on a missing/tampered seal or broken glass alone unless corroborated by the consumption pattern (no action if consumption exceeds ~75% of assessed), and the show-cause notice must precisely disclose the grounds relied on — failing which the assessment is set aside for breach of natural justice.
facts_squib: On inspection (29/08/2006) BSES found connected load 64.5 KW against 44 KW sanctioned, with tampered plastic/meter seals and scratches on the CT box; it issued a same-day show-cause notice and a bill of Rs 26,61,507 for DAE. The consumer challenged by writ, arguing seal irregularity alone could not prove DAE and that the consumption-pattern basis (alleged two-shift use) was never disclosed to him.
disposition: Writ petition allowed; BSES directed to issue a fresh notice disclosing all grounds (including the consumption pattern), grant a reasonable hearing, and pass a speaking order; a fresh bill may issue on the outcome.
procedural_posture: Writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution
relief_granted: Show-cause notice / bill process set aside; remitted for a fresh notice disclosing grounds, hearing, and speaking order.
amendment_considered: pre-2007 — the judgment reproduces Section 126(6) 'one-and-half times' and the 3/6-month presumption in Section 126(5), i.e. the text before Act 26 of 2007 (in force 15 June 2007)

regulations_construed.reg: DERC (Performance Standards Metering and Billing) Regulations, 2002, Reg. 25 (booking a case for pilferage/DAE)
DERC Regulations, 2002, Reg. 26 (personal hearing; consumption-pattern threshold)

provision_holdings.holding: An assessment for unauthorised use / DAE must be preceded by inspection and a reasonable hearing; the licensee is bound by the principles of natural justice (Section 126(3) read with Reg. 25(viii)).
provision_holdings.key_para: The licensee is obliged to follow principles of natural justice, and grant reasonable hearing

provision_holdings.holding: A suspicion of unauthorised use / DAE must be corroborated by the consumer's consumption pattern; that corroboration is a precondition to the exercise of assessment jurisdiction, and where consumption exceeds ~75% of the assessed figure no action can be taken. A missing seal or broken glass alone will not do.
provision_holdings.key_para: The object of obliging the assessing authority to ensure that consumption pattern, corroborates the suspicion of unauthorized use/ DAE, is a precondition for exercise of jurisdiction; if the consumption is more than 75% of the load, no action can be taken.

provision_holdings.holding: The show-cause notice must precisely and unambiguously state the allegations on which action is proposed; a notice that keeps the real basis (here, the consumption-pattern / two-shift-use finding) from the consumer fails the standard of fairness.
provision_holdings.key_para: Notice is not a ritualistic formality; the person requiring to show cause has to be precisely informed, may be briefly, the allegations upon which action is proposed.

authorities.name: Prakash Kumar v. State of Gujarat
authorities.principle: Stringent / penal statutes are to be strictly and purposively construed so that the legislative object is not frustrated.
authorities.principle_para: The more stringent the law, the less is the discretion of the Court.

authorities.name: Food Corporation of India v. State
authorities.principle: Natural justice requires that a person be given precise and adequate notice of the case to be met.

authorities.name: Canara Bank v. Debasish Das
authorities.principle: To the same effect on the requirement of a precise, adequate show-cause notice.

ratio.proposition: In a Section 126 unauthorised-use / DAE proceeding the show-cause notice must precisely disclose the grounds — including the consumption-pattern basis relied on — and the licensee must grant a real hearing; a demand founded on seal/glass irregularities without that disclosure or corroboration is set aside and remitted.

Corroboration of suspected unauthorised use / DAE by the consumer's consumption pattern (Reg. 26(ii)) is a precondition to the exercise of the assessing officer's jurisdiction; if consumption exceeds the prescribed threshold, no case can be booked.

significance: A frequently-cited (59×) Delhi single-judge authority on the procedural / natural-justice safeguards in Section 126 unauthorised-use (DAE) assessments: seal or glass irregularities alone cannot found a demand without consumption-pattern corroboration, and the show-cause notice must spell out the grounds. Decided on the pre-2007 Section 126 text (1.5× multiplier; 3/6-month presumption).

per_issue.natural-justice: good-law on the notice-specificity and hearing requirements.
per_issue.burden-proof: good-law on the consumption-pattern corroboration precondition.

validity.note: Not overruled. It applies the PRE-2007 Section 126 text (1.5× and 3/6-month presumption), later amended to 2× and a 12-month presumption — so do not cite it for the multiplier/period. The natural-justice and corroboration ratios are unaffected by the amendment.
